argument_summary: The present record supports certification only as a qualified certification, not as caveat-free compliance. Aggregate readiness passes by 2.4 percentage points and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which is sufficient evidence of operational readiness. The same record also shows a remaining below-target health-plan benefits support gap, concentrated in benefits-eligibility explanation, and a draft mitigation runbook that still lacks required governance elements. Under the stated policy, those facts do not support a no-material-limitation position. The defensible interpretation is therefore that the certification decision can be treated as supportable if and only if the unresolved limitation is explicitly preserved and disclosed in the certification artifact, rather than treated as resolved.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is narrower than a blanket bar on certification. It distinguishes caveat-free certification from certification with disclosed limitations. It says certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. It also says draft runbooks and monitoring do not remove a current disclosure requirement unless approved. On this record, policy does not support unconditional certification, but it does support a caveated certification posture if the unresolved named-use-case limitation is explicitly disclosed and preserved.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to justify the position. The evidence already supports a narrower path that preserves launch readiness while avoiding an unsupported clean-compliance assertion. Treating the packet as caveated rather than escalated is the lowest-friction position consistent with the admissible record.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the draft runbook has the required finalized owner and customer-notice criteria.
There is no admissible basis for claiming there are no known material limitations.
A clean certification finding would overstate what the present record supports.
